title: TCP 滑动窗口流量控制与零窗口探测
expected_output:
=== sliding window flow control: the sender is limited by rwnd ===
segment = 500 B; sender still owes bytes 500 .. 10999 (21 segments, so the data NEVER runs out)
round  rwnd   base  inflight            sent this round  unsent
    0  1500    500      1500              500,1000,1500    9000
    1  1500   2000      1500             2000,2500,3000    7500
    2  1000   3500      1000                  3500,4000    6500
    3  1000   4500      1000                  4500,5000    5500
    4     0   5500         0                    NOTHING    5500   <- TRUE ZERO WINDOW: data remains, but rwnd = 0
    5   500   5500       500                       5500    5000

reading the table:
  inflight = nxt - base never exceeds rwnd -> rwnd is the binding constraint
  round 4: rwnd = 0 -> NOTHING sent even though 5500 B are still waiting
           that is the genuine zero-window stall; a persist timer keeps probing
  unsent = 5000 at the end -> the stall was caused by the WINDOW, not by lack of data

=== zero-window deadlock avoidance ===
  receiver advertises rwnd=0
  sender stops, but starts a PERSIST TIMER
  on expiry it sends a 1-byte ZERO WINDOW PROBE
  receiver answers with the current rwnd (still 0 or reopened)
  without this probe, both sides would wait forever = DEADLOCK

=== silly window syndrome (SWS) ===
  receiver advertises tiny windows -> sender emits tiny segments -> overhead explodes
  receiver side fix (Clark): advertise only when window >= min(MSS, buffer/2)
  sender side fix (Nagle): buffer small writes, send only when a full MSS is ready
     (but always send the last buffered byte without waiting)
code:
SEG = 500
NSEG = 21
FIRST_SEQ = SEG                                  # 500
LAST_SEQ = FIRST_SEQ + (NSEG - 1) * SEG          # 10500 (last segment's seq)
END_SEQ = LAST_SEQ + SEG                         # 11000, one past the last byte
rwnd_schedule = {0: 1500, 1: 1500, 2: 1000, 3: 1000, 4: 0, 5: 500}

print("=== sliding window flow control: the sender is limited by rwnd ===")
print(f"segment = {SEG} B; sender still owes bytes {FIRST_SEQ} .. {END_SEQ - 1} "
      f"({NSEG} segments, so the data NEVER runs out)")

base = FIRST_SEQ      # oldest unacknowledged byte (0..499 was already acked)
nxt = FIRST_SEQ       # next sequence number to send
print(f"{'round':>5} {'rwnd':>5} {'base':>6} {'inflight':>9} {'sent this round':>26} {'unsent':>7}")

for rnd in sorted(rwnd_schedule):
    rwnd = rwnd_schedule[rnd]
    window_end = base + rwnd                 # send window is [base, base + rwnd)
    sent = []
    while nxt < window_end and nxt <= LAST_SEQ:
        sent.append(nxt)
        nxt += SEG
    label = ",".join(str(x) for x in sent) if sent else "NOTHING"
    note = "   <- TRUE ZERO WINDOW: data remains, but rwnd = 0" if rwnd == 0 else ""
    print(f"{rnd:>5} {rwnd:>5} {base:>6} {nxt - base:>9} {label:>26} {END_SEQ - nxt:>7}{note}")
    if sent:
        base = nxt                           # receiver ACKs all of them -> window slides

print()
print("reading the table:")
print("  inflight = nxt - base never exceeds rwnd -> rwnd is the binding constraint")
print(f"  round 4: rwnd = 0 -> NOTHING sent even though {END_SEQ - 5500} B are still waiting")
print("           that is the genuine zero-window stall; a persist timer keeps probing")
print(f"  unsent = {END_SEQ - 6000} at the end -> the stall was caused by the WINDOW, not by lack of data")

print()
print("=== zero-window deadlock avoidance ===")
print("  receiver advertises rwnd=0")
print("  sender stops, but starts a PERSIST TIMER")
print("  on expiry it sends a 1-byte ZERO WINDOW PROBE")
print("  receiver answers with the current rwnd (still 0 or reopened)")
print("  without this probe, both sides would wait forever = DEADLOCK")
print()
print("=== silly window syndrome (SWS) ===")
print("  receiver advertises tiny windows -> sender emits tiny segments -> overhead explodes")
print("  receiver side fix (Clark): advertise only when window >= min(MSS, buffer/2)")
print("  sender side fix (Nagle): buffer small writes, send only when a full MSS is ready")
print("     (but always send the last buffered byte without waiting)")
